question: The number of Barr corpuscles of the cells of a man with karyotype 48, XXXY is:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Karyotype 48, XXXY" -> "Presence of four sex chromosomes" -> "Two X chromosomes contribute to Barr bodies" -> "One Y chromosome does not contribute to Barr bodies" -> "Total Barr bodies = 2" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Karyotype 48, XXXY" -> "Three X chromosomes present" -> "Each X chromosome typically forms a Barr body" -> "One X chromosome remains active" -> "Total Barr bodies = 2" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Karyotype 48, XXXY" -> "Three X chromosomes" -> "Barr bodies formed from inactivated X chromosomes" -> "Two X chromosomes inactivated" -> "Total Barr bodies = 2" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Karyotype 48, XXXY" -> "Three X chromosomes" -> "Barr bodies are formed from excess X chromosomes" -> "Two Barr bodies formed" -> "Total Barr bodies = 2" -> 90%
analysis: In a male with a karyotype of 48, XXXY, there are two X chromosomes and one Y chromosome. Barr bodies are inactivated X chromosomes, and typically, one Barr body is formed for each additional X chromosome beyond one. Therefore, in this case, there would be one Barr body from the two X chromosomes present.
